task: datagrid_resize_drag_conflict
summary: Fixed DataGrid column resize handles triggering column move instead of resize. Root cause: resize handle pointerdown called stopPropagation() but not preventDefault(), so HTML5 drag-and-drop on the parent draggable=true cell still fired. Fix: added preventDefault() to resize handle pointerdown, and added dragstart guard to cancel drag when initiated from .datagrid-resize-handle. Also added sizeHint column option (xs/s/m/l/xl → 60/100/160/240/360px) that sets initial width and minWidth. ADR-109.

task: symbolpicker_insert_dismiss_fix

(2) SymbolPicker.insertSymbol() never called closePopup() after onInsert callback — added closePopup() call (no-op for inline mode).

task: graphcanvas_edge_label_density_hub_compact
summary: Fixed GraphCanvas hub-node edge label stacking (P2 per specs/2026-04-21-graphcanvas-edge-label-stacking-at-hubs.md, ADR-127). Root cause: renderEdgeLabel placed every label at Bézier midpoint t=0.5; the existing perpendicular offset only separates parallel edges between the same node pair, so hub→neighbor edges piled on top of each other when layouts clustered neighbors on one side. Added `edgeLabelDensity: 'all' | 'hub-compact' | 'none'` (default 'hub-compact') and `hubDegreeThreshold` (default 5) to GraphCanvasOptions. Hub-incident edges render a 2–3 char abbreviation on canvas (multi-word → word initials; single-word → first two chars, uppercased), full label still surfaced via edge HoverCard on hover. All label placement now runs through a greedy collision-avoidance loop stepping the Bézier parameter t outward from 0.5 through a fixed candidate list (0.5, 0.45, 0.55, 0.4, 0.6, …); bbox estimated as len*fontSize*0.6 so it works under jsdom. Falls back to midpoint if nothing fits (no hiding). Legacy `showEdgeLabels: false` still forces density 'none' for backward compat. New CSS hooks: .gc-edge-label and .gc-edge-label-compact. 13 new tests (graphcanvas-edge-labels.test.ts), full suite 3,893 / 3,893 green.

task: DynamicCanvas click-to-place: the canvas resolves a click into an anchor and records it (ADR-145 amended)
summary: startPlacement() arms the canvas; the user's next click resolves to a target node and a fractional spot within its scrollable content, and is emitted as an ordinary patch. The owner's rule: an app must not have to do extra work to use a component — persisting the document is the app's job, translating screen coordinates is not. Capture and restore are written adjacent as explicit inverses (capture divides out zoom, restore works in layout px). `within` names which scrolling region the fraction was measured against, so a component that scrolls internally is handled as well as one whose frame body takes the overflow; one capture-phase scroll listener catches every region, including ones created after mount. Known limit: a geometric anchor survives scrolling and resizing but not reflow; content anchoring is unbuilt. task: Visual refresh — tonal surface ladder, state layers, two-layer shadows, 4px radius, inset tab indicator (ADR-147)
summary: Five Material Design 3 ideas adopted at the token layer without adopting MD3. The flatness had a measurable cause rather than a stylistic one: --theme-body-bg and --theme-surface-bg both held #f8fafc, so the page had no ground and a sidebar was separated from the content beside it by a 1px border alone. Both themes now carry a four-step tonal ladder; the light-mode direction (raised is DARKER than surface) is preserved because 140 call sites depend on it. Hover and active became translucent state layers, without which the ladder does not survive contact — an opaque grey hover punches a hole in any surface that is not that exact grey. Shadows became two layers at lower alpha; the values are duplicated as Sass $shadow-* and CSS --theme-shadow-* and each now carries a note that the other exists. The tab indicator became a 3px pseudo-element inset 6px from the tab edges, and moved off a hardcoded $blue-600 that had made it inert in dark mode. Radius went to 4/2/6/8 by role, which amends the AGENTS.md 0-2 rule rather than contradicting it. Spacing was deliberately the smallest change: $spacer does not drive the $sp-* scale or control heights, so a global bump moves layouts unevenly; four reading-density values were raised instead. Two latent defects fixed: --theme-primary-rgb held Tailwind blues in both themes that do not match $primary, tinting every focus ring and glow off-hue, and --theme-surface-bg-rgb had drifted. TWO CONTRAST REGRESSIONS were introduced by this work and caught only by computing every text-on-surface pair in a browser, AFTER a draft of the spec had already claimed from reasoning that no ratio was reduced — that claim was wrong. Muted text on the darker ground fell to 3.94:1 (it had been 4.54:1, already marginal and unchecked) and the newly tinted active tab label measured 3.91:1 on chrome. Fixed by darkening --theme-text-muted to #556478 and adding --theme-primary-text (blue-700/blue-300) for primary carrying type. Verified 2026-09-08: 4825 unit tests across 142 files, structure checks PASSED, npm run build exit 0, measured ladder monotonic in both themes with all remaining pairs 9.15-17.56. Playwright still cannot run here (DEBT-WEB-3), so appearance is reviewed by eye against demo/visual-refresh.html.

task: Visual refresh round two — Bootstrap layer wired to the ladder, 51 hardcoded radius sites swept, DynamicCanvas token-name bug (ADR-147 amendment)
summary: Round one was reviewed as 'only a slight difference overall', with ribbon controls, dropdowns and the Dynamic UI DataGrid reported still square. Both correct, and the spec's claim that the change lands in two files was optimistic — it described where the tokens live, not where they are consumed. Four causes, all consumers that never received the tokens. $body-bg still compiled to $gray-50, so Bootstrap painted the page the OLD ground while every component used the new one, and the dark --bs-* surface overrides were pinned to raw greys off the ladder. Bootstrap has its OWN $box-shadow scale which was never overridden: dropdowns and modals draw from it rather than $shadow-*, so the most visible overlays in the library kept the single-blur smudge — the 'nice' dropdown shadows noted in review were in fact the old style. Ribbon pinned 17 call sites to a local $ribbon-ctrl-border-radius: 0, and 34 further sites hardcoded border-radius: 0, several with comments actively enforcing the dead rule. And dynamiccanvas.scss referenced var(--theme-border, ...) and var(--theme-surface, ...) — NEITHER TOKEN EXISTS, the real names being --theme-border-color and --theme-surface-bg — so it had been resolving to its hardcoded fallbacks and never participated in the theme in either mode; a custom-property fallback fails silently by design, which is why nothing caught it. Fixed by declaring the ladder once as Sass variables and interpolating into the CSS tokens, pointing the Bootstrap variables and shadow scale at the same values, and assigning 51 radius sites by role with three staying 0 deliberately and now documenting why. AuthCard's card was var(--bs-body-bg), the page ground, so it was the same colour as the page behind it. Verified 2026-09-08: --bs-body-bg and --theme-body-bg agree in both themes where they previously drifted, --bs-box-shadow is two-layer, ladder monotonic both directions, worst text-on-surface pair 5.00 light / 5.72 dark against a 4.5 floor, 4825 unit tests across 142 files, structure PASSED, build exit 0. task: Visual refresh round three — dark elevation rebuilt on light rings, 163 radius-by-omission sites, type and spacing bump (ADR-147 amendment 2)
summary: Three reported problems with three different causes. (1) Dark mode had no visible elevation, and raising alpha could never have fixed it: a black shadow on the #0d1420 ground reaches 1.034 contrast at alpha 0.22 and only 1.106 at 0.75, while a light-mode shadow at 0.08 already reaches 1.192. The ground is near-black so a darker shadow has nowhere to go — physics, not tuning. Every dark elevation now leads with a hairline light ring. Two further gaps went with it: --bs-box-shadow was compiled statically from the LIGHT values and never redefined in the dark block, so Bootstrap dropdowns and modals cast light-tinted shadows on a dark ground; and --theme-edge-shadow-color, the _chrome.scss docked-panel mixins, was black at 0.25 and equally invisible, now a faint lit seam. (2) Radius by omission: round two swept the 51 components that SET border-radius: 0, but the larger group was 71 components that never declared a radius at all and so rendered square whatever the token said. The reported split — line width picker sharp beside a rounded cron picker — is hand-rolled DOM versus Bootstrap-primitive-based components, which inherited the refresh for free. 163 rules across 46 components now take a radius by role, with layouts, full-bleed bars and text renderers deliberately excluded and drag handles denied by name. (3) Type: $font-size-sm carries 481 call sites against base's 201, so it and not base decides whether the interface reads small; sm 12.8->13.6, base 14->15, lg 16->17, with xs and 2xs held because 12px at line-height 1.45 needs 17.4px against a 16px ribbon label row. Control heights grew 2px since 15px text needs a 21.75px line box. $spacer 12->13px, $sp-* internals unchanged. Verified in a browser: LineWidthPicker trigger 4px and dropdown 6px with shadow, ProgressModal 6px, ribbon buttons and tabs 4px, and ZERO vertical overflow anywhere in the ribbon at the larger type — the only machine check available while Playwright e2e cannot run (DEBT-WEB-3). 4825 unit tests across 142 files, structure PASSED, build exit 0.

task: Repaired agentknowledge/history.jsonl and added a parse guard (DEBT-KB-1)
summary: history.jsonl had been invalid JSONL since February and nobody noticed for six months, because nothing ever parsed it. Three lines failed json.loads from two distinct causes, both from writing JSON with shell text tools rather than a serializer: two entries were appended WITHOUT a trailing newline so the next append landed on the same line, giving ..."}{"date":..., introduced in 9c9be2e; and one carried \!, which is not a valid JSON escape and is the signature of bash history-expansion escaping leaking through a double-quoted append, introduced in 3020cd5. Repaired by splitting the two joined lines and unescaping the one bad escape: 241 non-empty lines to 243, byte count +1 (two newlines added, one backslash removed), and a SHA-256 of both files with newlines and the escape normalised away is IDENTICAL, proving only framing changed and no content was lost. Prevention rather than just repair: test-local.sh check [8] now parses history.jsonl and all three YAML files on every npm test, and was mutation-tested by corrupting a copy to confirm it fails rather than merely passing on a good file; AGENTS.md now requires appending with a JSON serializer and says why. Also closed out ADR-147 standards work: added SurfaceLadder, StateLayer and ElevationScale concepts, updated the stale EnterpriseTheme concept which still described the theme as square with zero border radius, promoted the one raw hex introduced outside the palette to a named $gray-550, corrected its ordering in the ramp, refreshed the _variables.scss header marker which still said 'square', fixed two non-Allman braces in the demo page, and recorded DEBT-VR-1 through DEBT-VR-4.

task: ADR-148 — a component that cannot read must refuse, not fabricate; twelve sites closed and a build guard added
summary: Two bug reports from the consuming apps repo after a production data-loss incident: a mock graph answered serialize() with an empty document and the autosave wrote it over live sessions. The reports named four pickers; an audit of all 125 components found TWELVE sites across SEVEN components, including three the reports did not reach and one they explicitly cleared. The two that mattered most were both missed. DynamicFormSwitcher is the AGGREGATION POINT — AGENTS.md designates it the generic form host every value-bearing component flows through — and its readFieldValue converted an adapter throw into undefined while fallbackDefault invented a typed value for an unmounted field, both feeding getValues(), which is what a host passes to api.save(); fixing the five pickers without it would have accomplished nothing, because a picker's throw was caught there and reconverted into a fabrication. prompttemplatemanager's save path was the most damaging single site: a rejected save called replaceTemplate with the local copy, then ran clearDirty UNCONDITIONALLY and logged 'Saved', so the editor showed the work as saved, dropped the unsaved marker, and the user navigated away and lost it with no error at the point of loss. Also corrected the report on layoutpicker, cleared as not-a-problem: its getValue returned null against a LayoutAlgorithm|null contract, so null is a legitimate 'nothing selected' and the stand-in was indistinguishable from a real choice. Two tests were asserting the defect — columnspicker and spacingpicker required getValue().name to equal the fabricated preset after a failed mount, the exact shape the report warned about while saying 'yours is not that' — and layoutpicker had no test file at all. The permitting instruction was not the contradiction the reports expected: this repo has neither conflicting line, only FRONTEND.md:87 'log the error and leave the DOM unchanged', which is incomplete rather than wrong and licenses the null object by omission. Fixes: five pickers throw and their null factories are deleted (no internal caller affected, all in-repo references are registry name strings); getValues/getAllValues refuse and name unreadable fields, with an UNREADABLE unique symbol distinguishing 'could not read' from the undefined/null/empty-string a form may legitimately hold, chosen by the user over two weaker options; three prompttemplatemanager callback paths keep prior state and surface the error; recents caches may read empty but no longer write back. scripts/check-stand-in-reads.py runs as structure check [9] and is mutation-tested; its header states what it cannot see, and a catch-block regex producing 25 hits of which ~4 were real was dropped rather than shipped as noise. ConfirmDialog was checked against the reports' open question and fails VISIBLE rather than invisible-but-clickable. Dependency-closure request deferred as DEBT-SEC-4, DOMPurify first. Verified 2026-10-04: 4842 unit tests across 143 files (+17, +1), 21/21 structure checks, build exit 0.

task: ADR-149 — serve four closed dependencies at immutable URLs with SRI (DEBT-SEC-4, first slice)
summary: First slice of the apps team's dependency-closure request. dompurify, maxgraph, signalr and cytoscape now build to single self-contained files at /lib/<name>-<version>.js with an SRI manifest at /lib-manifest.json. THE PRIORITY ASSET WAS ITSELF VULNERABLE: the report said do DOMPurify first because a substituted sanitizer becomes the attack, and pinning the apps' 3.2.4 to vendor it put it under our npm audit for the first time, surfacing NINETEEN open advisories against that version including XSS bypasses — it did not need substituting. Vendored at 3.4.16; the other three are clean at the versions the apps use. Closure is ASSERTED from esbuild's metafile rather than grepped: a regex for dynamic import() over the minified maxGraph bundle gave three false positives from a class method named 'import', while the metafile reports 240 inputs and zero externals authoritatively; the assertion was proved to fire by rebuilding the same entry with --external. vditor is DEFERRED because it cannot satisfy the one-file constraint — it hardcodes unpkg.com as its sub-resource CDN and lazily fetches from a 21MB dist/js tree (echarts, mermaid, katex, mathjax and more), injecting those chunks with no integrity attribute, which is exactly the one-level-down hole the report names; three options recorded in the spec. Headers: /lib/* is immutable for a year since the version is in the path, with Access-Control-Allow-Origin required rather than cosmetic because SRI forces crossorigin=anonymous; the manifest sits outside /lib/ so the patterns stay disjoint, per the warning in cdn/_headers that Cloudflare emits every matching rule. Structure check [10] re-pairs each published hash with its artifact and is mutation-tested. Also upgraded postcss-cli 11 to 12, clearing three high advisories published against existing tooling since the last audit — verified unrelated to this branch by auditing main's lockfile, and compiled custom.css is byte-identical across the upgrade. task: CDN Integration Guide written and referenced; fixed seven unpublished docs and three broken links in the published index

task: DEBT-SEC-6 resolved — version skew settled by measurement; font-awesome and chart.js vendored, bootstrap-icons shown unnecessary
summary: The remaining closure work was recorded as 'decisions that are partly theirs'. task: DEBT-SEC-5 resolved — vditor's full dependency tree served from this origin; the request's last open item closes
summary: The spec recorded vditor as needing a decision from the apps team about setting its `cdn` option. Reading their code first showed the decision was not theirs: THE APPS NEVER INSTANTIATE VDITOR. They use this library's createMarkdownEditor, which wraps it — so the unpkg.com fetches were ours to stop, and the fix needs no consuming app change at all. vditor hardcodes CDN='https://unpkg.com/vditor@3.11.2' and lazily fetches its markdown engine (lute, 3.9MB), icon set, language pack and every optional renderer — mermaid, katex, mathjax, graphviz, echarts — as script tags it injects itself; our buildVditorOptions never set `cdn`, so all of that was executable third-party code arriving on pages that may show an admin session. The whole dist tree is now served at /lib/vditor-3.11.2/ with types/ and ts/ excluded (typings and sources, never fetched), and MarkdownEditor sets `cdn` to it, derived from the serving script's own origin via document.currentScript so a fork or local build works rather than hardcoding one domain into a component others deploy; the catch branch falls back to a same-origin relative path and never to a public CDN. Serving only the always-needed subset was rejected: it saves ~16MB and breaks silently the first time a user writes a mermaid block, and lute being always required meant the subset was never small. Verified vditor builds sub-resource URLs as ${cdn}/dist/js/... before relying on the layout. A regression test asserts the cdn option is set and contains neither unpkg nor jsdelivr, mutation-tested by commenting the line out. KNOWN RESIDUAL recorded rather than hidden: the injected chunks carry no SRI because vditor injects them itself. Deploy grows to 41MB across 1137 files, within the Workers 20000-file limit with the largest single file at 3.9MB against a 25MiB cap. Verified 2026-10-04: 7 vendored artifacts match their hashes, 23/23 structure checks, build exit 0.

task: ADR-150 — widened the surface ladder and tinted chrome so panels read as a different material
summary: Side panels, top bars and status bars were reported as poorly differentiated. Measurement made it precise: chrome against content was 1.056 where 1.000 means identical, so a sidebar was separated from the document almost entirely by its 1px border; dark was 1.151, which is why it read as a light-mode problem. Two faults in the ADR-147 ladder. It separated planes by LUMINANCE ALONE — saturation never exceeded 0.33 across all four surfaces, so every plane was the same near-neutral material at a different brightness. And it had run out of room: four steps packed between #e6eaf1 and white, chrome sitting 0.051 of luminance below content and 0.051 above ground. Tinting chrome alone was tried FIRST and fails — chrome moves down into the ground step and chrome|ground collapses from 1.055 to 1.013 — so the whole ladder had to widen. Chrome now carries a low-saturation cast toward the primary, the one Material Design 3 idea in play, so it reads as a different MATERIAL rather than a dimmer white. $gray-550 darkened again from #556478 to #4d5b6d because the widened ladder puts the darkest light surface at #d8e2ee where the old value measured 4.61, passing AA by hundredths — the exact state that broke when a background last moved (AGENT_INSIGHTS 6.8); it measures 5.29 there now. Separation was judged on the adjacencies that OCCUR ON SCREEN rather than every pair: sunken|ground measures only 1.040 in dark and that is fine because wells sit inside content and never against the page ground, so optimising it would have cost contrast elsewhere for nothing. Verified in a browser against the built stylesheet — chrome|content 1.108 light / 1.240 dark, chrome|ground 1.085 / 1.383, sunken|content 1.310 / 1.160, worst text 5.29 / 5.20 against a 4.5 floor, luminance ordering monotonic in both themes so the 140 direction-dependent call sites are unaffected. A measurement bug in the checker itself was caught and fixed mid-verification: the browser returns #fff shorthand for white and the hex parser assumed six digits, returning null for two light adjacencies. 23/23 structure checks, 4842 tests, build exit 0.

task: DEBT-VR-5 resolved — automated surface-contrast gate as structure check [12]

task: ADR-151 — contrast measured against composited backgrounds; eight shipped AA failures fixed
summary: Check [12] measured text against the four FLAT surfaces and passed cleanly while eight pairs sat below the 4.5 AA floor in shipped CSS. The reason is that the state layers are translucent: what a user sees is the layer composited over whatever surface is beneath it, and NO TOKEN NAMES that colour, so a token-by-token audit cannot examine it. The worst was confirmed concretely rather than inferred — toolbar.scss:581 sets color: var(--theme-text-muted) and :586 sets &:hover { background-color: var(--theme-active-bg) } on the SAME element over chrome, so hovering a toolbar button in dark mode put its own label at 3.69; 21 sites across the fleet pair a state layer with muted text. The gate now composites every layer over every surface against every text token, 96 pairs per run, checked STRICTLY rather than against a usage map — the user chose strict when the costs were presented, on the grounds that a map goes stale silently when a component moves surfaces and a stale map makes the gate confidently wrong. An unparseable layer now FAILS rather than being skipped, because the first implementation skipped silently and a skipped case is indistinguishable from a passing one. THE ACCEPTED COST WAS NOT PAID: reaching zero appeared to require softening the state layers ~25%, which was costed and accepted, but measuring that consequence first showed light hover on chrome would fall to 1.072 against the 1.056 that prompted the original complaint — trading an AA failure for an invisible hover — and re-solving with the layers held fixed showed three text-token changes alone clear all 96 pairs. task: ADR-152 — light backgrounds surviving into dark mode in VisualTableEditor presets and three demo pages
summary: Two defects reported from the demo gallery, one shape: a light background applied as a FIXED value while the text colour came from the theme, so in dark mode the text inverted, the background did not, and the content vanished. Each literal preset now declares a dark twin at the same hue (#e7f1ff->#1d2735, #f8f9fa->#222930, #e8f5e9->#1d351e, #fff3e0->#352c1d) and the colours reach CSS as --vte-alt-row / --vte-alt-row-dark custom properties the stylesheet switches on [data-bs-theme], so a toggle repaints with no re-render; a preset with no dark twin falls back to the themed sunken surface rather than the light literal, which would reproduce the defect. Verified in a browser: 23 alternating rows readable in both themes AND carrying genuinely different backgrounds per theme rather than an absence of tint, three stepper panes readable in both. A regression test asserts a literal-tint preset declares a dark twin and never pins an inline background, mutation-tested by reverting the apply path. Stated limits: delta-E 10 is a rule of thumb for side-by-side swatches not a standard, it says nothing about thin lines or small dots, and it does NOT discharge WCAG 1.4.1 — colour must still not be the only channel. THE ELEVATION CHECKER NEEDED THREE FIXES WHILE THE THEME WAS CORRECT THROUGHOUT, each reading as a real failure: a missing re.M made ^ match only the file start and reported every declaration absent; a flat dict kept the DARK --theme-shadow-* because _dark-mode.scss declares them twice, so the Sass scale was compared against values that legitimately differ; and an alpha regex using [^)]* stopped at the ) inside var(.
